This method is much easier than the currently existing methods using linear programming and the performance is satisfied. More importantly, the overall complex errors are also equiripple in the complex Chebyshev sense. This approach has several practical advantages such as fast design time and easy implementation with comparable accuracy. Numerical design examples including a lowpass filter and sine-delay FIR allpass phase equalizers are given to show the effectiveness of this approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A circuit theory of computations
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An attempt is made to develop a stable and numerically robust calculus for matrices and operators, with reduced or minimal complexity. The author starts by developing a time-varying calculus, where instantaneous operations are characterized and a generalization of the z-transform to express divisibility and rational calculus is found. Next, the author defines scattering operators and orthogonal filters, and develops a method of approximations leading to optimal filter synthesis and linking the two previous items.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An effective data structure for VLSI layout systems
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An effective data structure is presented which is called a B-2 tree (bucket tree with 2-D binary trees) suitable for VLSI layout systems. The B-2 tree consists of a main binary tree which forms a directory for buckets, and bisector lists with 2-D binary trees. Experimental results have shown that the B-2 tree is superior to other data structures in region search performance even for huge size data. It has also been shown that its region search performance is not influenced by the distribution of objects on a chip.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Latched differential FET logic
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new circuit topology is proposed for creating complex logic circuits in GaAs. Latched differential FET logic (LDFL) is a fully differential logic family that provides complex logic function capability, tolerance to threshold voltage variations, and complementary, latched-function outputs. LDFL is capable of performing up to eleven levels of logic in one gate, while still giving excellent performance. LDFL also provides improved noise margins due to the use of bootstrapped loads and significantly reduces the load-to-logic ratioing constraint. A nine-level LDFL gate has a delay of 1.7 ns and a static power dissipation of 4 mW as demonstrated in simulations of 4-bit digital comparator circuits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Estimation of energy distributions in generalized multi-element-kind systems
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A general method for estimating energy distribution in multi-element-kind systems with arbitrary circuit topology is presented. Bounds on the power dissipation in various two-terminal elements are computed for exponentially damped sinusoidal excitations under steady state. The proposed algorithm is not only limited to single-frequency excitations, but applies equally to harmonic analysis associated with exponentially damped periodic excitations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: GaAs FET physical modeling and optimization
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present a modified version of the PHYSGEN model developed by M.A. Khatibzadeh and R.J. Trew (see IEEE Trans. Microwave Theory Tech., vol.36, p.231-238, Feb. 1988). The authors introduce three new parameters into the Khatibzadeh-Trew model. The revised model also includes the effect of the parasitic resistances on the DC characteristics. The modified model accounts for the small signal behavior of actual devices. This improved model is then incorporated into an optimization routine to allow the designer to obtain a better match to measured data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Autopilot designs for BTT CLOS guidance
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Optimum autopilot designs are presented for bank-to-turn CLOS (BTT) guidance. BTT is capable of producing higher lift-to-drag ratio. A linear quadratic optimal technique is used for the design of the roll and pitch autopilot. Simulation results have demonstrated the improvements in control with the linear quadratic optimal design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modeling frequency responses by positive rational functions
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The problem of finding a rational function of a real variable interpolating at given points (with suitable intersection numbers) while being everywhere positive is considered. The positivity requirement is essential, e.g. in modeling the square magnitude of a frequency response. This goal is achieved by resorting to a Hermite-type approach which allows one to obtain positive interpolating functions of minimum complexity by means of an efficient numerical procedure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mozart-MM: A mixed-mode and multi-level simulation system
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors describe the Mozart-mixed mode (MM) simulation system which was formed by a tight coupling of the Mozart multi-level simulator and the Eldo analog simulator. Mozart-MM spans all the digital levels from behavioral to pseudo-electrical as well as the analog circuit and behavioral levels. This work required the development of a new algorithm to couple a digital simulator with discrete time together with a circuit simulator with adaptable time step. The full Mozart interactivity has been extended to Mozart-MM allowing the user to have direct control of the simulation experiment, including the possibility to conditionally execute commands. New techniques for netlisting, X handling and for the verification of the interface unidirectionally assumption are also presented. The tool has been tested extensively and the results presented demonstrate its performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel CMOS analog counter for Boltzmann machines
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A CMOS analog counter for artificial neural networks which is based on a novel principle of charge injection is described. It features an excellent linearity and controllability of its step in a large dynamic range. This counter circuit has a small area and a high robustness against device dispersion.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved problem formulation for signal extrapolation
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The extrapolation of a discrete-time signal is considered. Iterative algorithms for this problem require numerous iterations for accurate results. An analysis shows the very large condition number of the linear equations, and thus the slow convergence. One way to circumvent the slow convergence is to use better algorithms, such as truncated singular value decomposition (TSVD) or special conjugate gradient algorithms. An improved problem formulation is proposed. It is shown how to reduce the condition number by some orders of magnitude with a more realistic low-pass filter matrix. The modified system is solved by TSVD with uncritical dependence of the solution error on the number of singular values involved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Gradient algorithms for FIR adaptive filtering - A tutorial
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A unified approach for generating fast block- and sequential-gradient LMS FIR (least mean square finite impulse response) adaptive algorithms is presented. The general formulation leads to three classes of adaptive algorithms. It is shown how each class of algorithms is obtained from the previous one by a simple trade-off between adaptation performance and computational complexity. Implementation aspects of the generated algorithms are examined and their performance is evaluated and compared with that of several recently proposed algorithms by means of computer simulations under a wide range of adaptation conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New heuristics and lower bounds for graph partitioning
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Addresses the problem of partitioning the vertex set of an edge-weighted undirected graph into two parts of specified sizes so that the sum of the weights on edges joining vertices in different parts is minimum. The authors report on a new class of algorithms that solve the graph partitioning problem in polynomial time by using low-rank approximations of the connection matrix obtained from principal components analysis. These algorithms also provide a bound on the proximity of the cost of the constructed partition to the optimal cost based on the eigenvalues left out in the rank reduction process. The lower bounds derived are proven to be superior to the Donath-Hoffman lower bound for two significant special cases, wherein either the two part sizes are equal, or the graph connection matrix has equal row-sums. Simulation results for randomly constructed graphs of different sizes are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Error bounds of piecewise-linear approximation
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A description is given of upper bounds on the error caused by piecewise-linear approximation of a nonlinear element T in a feedback loop, where T represents a nonlinear operator whose domain is the set of the z-transform of the sampled sequences. Let W' (z) be the solution of W' (z)=X (z)+H (z) T' (W' (z)) which approximates the exact input-output relation W (z)=X (z)+H (z) T (W (z)). In order to discuss an upper bound on the norm of the approximation error // W' (z)-W (z) //, the generalized parametric norm of an operator is proposed. The obtained upper bound is sufficiently small compared with a bound by the conventional norm in many cases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A family of new Rudin's theorem type results for scattering Schur polynomials
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author proves a class of results which can be considered to be the scattering Schur counterpart of the Rudin type results well known in the context of strict sense Schur polynomials. These results establish that test for zeros of a multivariable polynomial in a polydisc can be equivalently broken up into a set of simpler tests, the latter tests being a search for zeros in domains which are subsets of the unit polydisc. The author classifies the results of the present work into two categories. Results of the first type require test for zeros of the polynomial on the distinguished boundary and a set of 1-D tests for zeros in the unit disc. Results of the second type require a test for zeros of the polynomial on the distinguished boundary and only one 1-D test in the unit disc.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Two architectures implementing feed-forward completely connected neural nets
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Feedforward completely-connected neural nets represent the most general scheme of loopless ANNs (artificial neural networks). Two architectures are presented. The second one (unfolded) presents a higher throughput (a higher number of shorter W-SRs) but a lower regularity (two different PEs, or processing elements); the first one (folded) presents a lower number of PEs (although more complex) and a higher regularity in the output signals ordered on the same output line from n/sub 0/ to n/sub N/.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improving performance of synthesis
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The importance of multiplexers and controller costs on the final area and speed of synthesized designs is demonstrated. In order to produce optimal results, these factors cannot be ignored. In addition, the authors demonstrate the tradeoff of single- versus multi-function ALUs on synthesis results. Including these factors during synthesis yields results which are both smaller and faster than those produced without them. The behavioral synthesis system has been modified to include these factors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Unstable vectors in Hopfield nets
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: It has been shown that the storage capacity of the Hopfield net is a function of the size of the network. However, it is also known that even if the number of input vectors is less than the maximum storage capacity of the network, incorrect associations can still occur. Such problems exist if these vectors have too large an overlap. The authors show some experimental results, as well as the mathematical analysis relating the stability of the input vectors to a similarity measure based on the Hamming distance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A stochastic model for fault propagation, in combinational circuits
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present a new stochastic model for fault propagation in combinational circuits that is sensitive to the structural characteristics of the circuit. Under random testing, fault propagation through a circuit is modeled as a branching process. Due to the presence of fanout, a fault on a gate at level l, once activated, will generate a number of copies of itself, called descendants, at level l+1. Similarly, due to the presence of reconvergent fanout, a fault may cease to propagate. An activated fault is detected if at least one of its descendants is active at the primary outputs. For a fault on a gate at level l, the authors present basic results on the distribution of the number of next-level descendants and the number of kth-level descendants, k>or=l. The importance of these results lies in the fact that they are sensitive to the circuit structure and play a basic role in design for testability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Parallelism of circuit simulation on array processor
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The intrinsic parallelism of circuit simulation techniques, especially the relaxation-based electrical simulation technique, is analyzed by the dependence graph (DG) representation. The results show that many proposed parallel schemes are the different mappings of these DGs. The hardware array processor architectures for an event-driven MOS timing simulator, EMOTA, are proposed and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis algorithm and automated reasoning method for fault analysis
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author develops an algorithm to study the concept of fault diagnosis in a system which has been designed for fault diagnosis without repair using the models developed independently by F.P. Preparata et al. (1967) and S.L. Hakimi and T. Amin (1974). Having developed the algorithm for fault diagnosis, one can perform the process of the fault analysis. It is also demonstrated that the algorithm is correct and general for the number of faults of the system. It is shown that the results of the artificial intelligence algorithm developed in the paper agree with those of Hakimi and Amin.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of acquisition in phase-locked loops incorporating phase-frequency detectors
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The time required for a phase-locked loop (PLL) to acquire lock is an important design parameter. Most modern PLLs incorporate a phase-frequency detector because out of lock it behaves as a frequency discriminator and aids acquisition. However, a correct analysis of the acquisition behavior of this type of loop has yet to be presented, mainly because of confusion regarding the pulse output duty cycle of the phase detector. The first correct analysis of the acquisition behavior is presented. The result is confirmed by simulation. Data are presented for both second- and third-order loops.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reality of chaos in four-dimensional hysteretic circuits
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Rigorous evidence for chaos in a certain class of four-dimensional hysteretic circuits is presented. The case in which a coefficient matrix has complex eigenvalues and can be transformed into a Jordan form is considered. The chaos-generating condition is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer-aided analysis of chaotic circuits and systems
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A multipurpose software package, NONLIN, is introduced for analyzing chaotic circuits and systems as a tool of computer-aided analysis. It consists of 7 functional modulars as follows: calculate and display trajectories, bifurcation diagrams, Poincare map and invariant manifold, calculate equilibrium points, periodic solutions and Lyapunov exponents. NONLIN can be used to analyze any (finite) order nonlinear differential equation. It is user-friendly, highly interactive, graphically oriented, and runs under the PC-DOS operating system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An adaptive image encoding technique using pyramid architecture
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An adaptive block truncation encoding scheme is described. The adaptive block size encoding approach used removes the bottlenecks of compromising the reduction factor and fidelity of the decoded image present in the corresponding fixed block size scheme. The results show that the adaptive scheme produces a better reduction ratio, keeping approximately the same fidelity measure. The scheme is suitable for implementation with the pyramidal architecture which has a hierarchical nature of processing and needs greatly reduced logarithmic distances for passing information among the processing elements of the meshes. An added advantage of the present system is that it extracts most of the edge information and localizes it at the lowest mesh with respect to the host. This simplifies greatly the further processing of the image regarding its edges and regions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of a practical algorithm for power system critical measurement by using network topology
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors reports on an implementation and testing of a practical algorithm for determining power system critical measurements based on network topology. The critical measurement algorithm is based on a practical observability algorithm modified to identify each critical measurement whose loss would render the network unobservable. A small power system network, the IEEE 14-bus network system, was used to test the algorithm for analysis of various measurement sets. A large power system network consisting of eighty buses and a hundred and ten lines was successfully tested in the industrial environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A continuous deformation method for resistive circuits containing active and non-reciprocal elements
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Globally convergent homotopy methods for solving nonlinear resistive circuits are based on assumptions that are justified in most circuits with independent sources and eventually passive resistors and, in particular, in common electronic circuits. At the same time however, these conditions for convergence exclude a lot of circuits with active elements such as operational amplifiers or controlled sources. This is a fundamental limitation common to all homotopy methods known in circuit theory. The algorithm of L. Vandenberghe and J. Vandewalle (1990) is extended in order to process a broad class of active circuits. The reflection steps described make it possible to apply the octahedral algorithm to a much broader class of circuits and to use the algorithm to find multiple solutions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System identification of linear continuous systems via the Gram matrix
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new method for system identification of linear continuous single-input-single-output (SISO) systems based on the Gram matrix is proposed. The proposed algorithm is based on some new properties of the Gram matrix derived in the paper based on the relationship between the Gram matrix and the impulse-response Gramian. It requires only the diagonal elements of the Gram matrix and the time moments, which can be easily obtained experimentally or can be computed from the impulse-response measurements. The method is shown to be computationally simpler than earlier methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the synthesis of variable sequential circuit
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A synthesis method for variable sequential circuits (VSCs) is discussed. The VSC corresponds to a multiple-output variable logic circuit (VLC) with some memory elements. Hence, the synthesis method for a VLC can be applied to VSC. The results of numerical experiments for synthesis methods are shown, and the effective method is proposed for the VSC. This method can also be applied to the VLC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An alternative combining architecture for large-scale shared-memory multiprocessors
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Investigates an alternative combining architecture for removing degradation of the multiprocessor interconnection network due to hot-spot contention, which results in drastically inferior performance. Based on a combining tree, the proposed combining architecture has much lower hardware complexity than the prior combining network and yet can effectively eliminate hot-spot contention. Simulation results confirm that the mean latency of hot-spot requests through the alternative combining architecture is low, provided that the concurrent hot-spot number is reasonably small (say, no more than 8). A fault-tolerant technique for the combining architecture is also addressed to significantly enhance its reliability at a little extra cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Using hybrid techniques for a continuous-time inference network
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A class of binary relation inference network was recently proposed for constraint-satisfaction applications, including time/location-referencing and air-traffic control problems. There are some intrinsic weaknesses underlying this type of discrete-time inference network, namely, network instability and oscillation under specific circumstances, and the slow convergence rate commonly observed in large networks. To circumvent the potential shortcomings of existing inference networks, state-space techniques are used to derive a more robust continuous-time inference network. Simulation studies on two hybrid implementations indicate significant improvements over discrete-time inference network, and demonstrate their practical viability for applications in time-varying cases.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modified polyphase filter structure for computing interpolated data as successive differential corrections
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A differential correction interpolating scheme is developed which computes successive first differences between adjacent output samples. This scheme obtains a specified system performance using filter coefficients with a reduced number of bits and consequently accommodates multipliers with reduced accuracy. This technique is easily extended to higher-order difference corrections to achieve further bit reductions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neural implementation of Karmarkar algorithm
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The Karmarkar algorithm performs a sequence of projective transformations each followed by optimization over an inscribed sphere and then inverse projective transformation. These steps are implemented on the authors' model with two neural-like circuits, one embedded inside the other. The inner circuit finds least square error solutions using the complementary slackness condition. The outer circuit finds a novel interior primal solution using the delta rule by making use of the error in the computation of dual solution. This circuit exhibits potential for applications where real-time optimization is required-as is the case in robotics, satellite guidance, etc.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Trilinear analysis applied to multichannel evoked potentials
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A method for applying the topographic components (TC) model to discrimination and classification of multichannel evoked potentials (MEPs) is proposed, and a study designed to demonstrate and test this method is presented. The TC model is used to compare the MEPs of 'normal' and 'abnormal' test subjects to those of a normal reference group, as might be done clinically to screen patients for pathology. The spatial/temporal components identified for the reference group are demonstrated to fit the MEPs of the normal test subjects (not part of the group to which the model was originally fit), but not those of the abnormal test subjects. It is concluded that the TC model can indeed be a useful tool in MEP classification, e.g. in clinical diagnosis, and that further study is warranted along these lines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Set-membership estimation for adaptive signal processing
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors give a brief overview of the problem of set-membership estimation in adaptive signal processing. Recently, there seems to be a resurgence of interest in these types of estimation schemes as they feature 100% confidence regions for parameter estimates. Some of these recursive schemes also feature selective updating. More recently, the systolic implementation and lattice structure of some particular schemes have also been investigated. Exact polytope bounding, orthotope bounding, and the OBE algorithms are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Matrix representation of operators in two-dimensional signal processing and its applications to picture processing
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The fundamentals of operator-algebraic treatment of two-dimensional (2-D) signal processing systems are established. Using several results concerning an operator corresponding to the impulse response of a 2-D system, it then becomes possible to handle the problems of analysis and synthesis of a 2-D system in picture or image signal processing.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Proof procedures and axiom set in Petri net models of Horn clause propositional logic
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors analyze the time complexities of (1) the provability detecting problem, (2) the minimum axiom set problem, and (3) the minimum variable deletion problem in the Horn clause propositional logic. An O( sigma ) algorithm for the first problem is proposed, where sigma is the formula size of a given set of Horn clauses. The second problem is shown to be NP-complete and some approximation algorithms with their experimental evaluation are given. Concerning the third problem, which has been known to be NP-complete, a number of new approximation algorithms with their experimental evaluation are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Counter reduction techniques for Hamming count
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Hardware overhead reduction through counter selection is considered for the Hamming count compaction test. A method to choose the most effective syndrome and input variable counter combination is introduced. Both simulation and theoretical analysis illustrate that the proposed method produces an optimal pairing. Adaptations in the counter selection method are made forming a greedy strategy for choosing multiple counters to combine with the syndrome counter. Complexity of both the single and multiple counter selection algorithms is very reasonable. The method promotes intelligent counter selection to minimize any impact test hardware reduction will have on fault detection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Precise range-ordering for dominant paths through interconnection networks
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new algorithm based upon the superposition principle and a novel decomposition technique for an interconnection network are developed and computer-coded. It determines the precise rank-ordering of all input-to-output transmission paths. The rank-ordering reveals the dominant paths and quantifies the relative importance of each path.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Programmable FIR switched-capacitor decimators
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A study is made of programmable switched-capacitor (SC) decimating structures with finite impulse response (FIR). Alternative structures are presented in which programmability is achieved using quasi-passive multiplying and algorithmic digital-to-analog converters. Their comparative advantages are outlined considering such design aspects as component count, capacitance spread, speed of operation, and complexity of the digital switching waveform generators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Statistically consistent frequency estimation using linear prediction
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new statistically consistent frequency estimation method has been developed and presented using linear prediction (LP) method. The observed signal is assumed to be a sum of complex exponentials with white random noise process. The number of complex exponentials is assumed to be known. A statistically consistent estimator is an estimator that converges to the true value as the number of observations increases to infinite. It is shown that conventional LP-based estimation methods such as Prony's method are not consistent statistically. It is also proved that the new estimation method provides statistically consistent estimates and performs better than Prony's estimation method. Numerical simulation is provided to confirm the performance of the new estimation method and its statistical consistency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Synthesis and analysis of 3D-images generated from contiguous slice-images obtained by confocal laser scanning microscopy
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An approach is described which consists of a combination of molecular probes and associated detection systems, confocal laser scanning microscopy, special segmentation and visualization techniques, and a workstation based on a transputer network for the synthesis and analysis of 3D images from a stack of contiguous slice images. Based on a slice-by-slice approach the proposed technique identifies 3D objects and transforms them into abstract data structures such as medial axis representations (MARs) or surface net representations. Solid modeling procedures then permit the visualization and quantification of the cell components described by such data structures. The main advantage of this setup is that each 3D object in the image volume is described by a unique MAR.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimization of multirate filter banks within the framework of a human visual model
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A perfect reconstruction filter optimization based on a human visual model is presented. The optimized filters are compared to a set of published filters for coding at a fixed bit rate. A method is suggested for adapting the filters to change in source statistics. This method is applied to coding of intraframe data and residual frame data after motion-compensated prediction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Cellular radio linear codec
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Designed specifically to satisfy the European cellular radio market, the ADSP28msp02 linear codec combines 16-bit analog/digital, 16-bit digital/analog with the appropriate anti-aliasing/anti-imaging filtering. Fabricated in a VLSI digital process with high linearity poly-poly capacitors, the msp02 contains >100 K transistors in an area <54 K mil/sup 2/ with a die aspect ratio allowing the part to be assembled in a 24-pin skinny package while running off a single 5-V supply. Two versions of the linear codec were fabricated and assembled: a monolithic, fully integrated part and a compound-monolithic, two-chip solution to facilitate investigation into the interaction between the digital and the analog circuitry. Evaluation results indicate that the part meets the requirements of the cellular radio market.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High performance GaAs analog sampled data circuits and systems
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The design of high-frequency GaAs analog sampled data systems using switched capacitor circuit techniques is reviewed including op-amp and switch design and optimization of the circuit for maximum clock-rate. A second order switched capacitor bandpass filter example with high precision measured response characteristics for a clock-rate of 500 MHz is discussed. Possible op-amp and switch designs to allow clock-rates around 1 GHz are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Accuracy and complexity in the modelling of power systems subject to large network disturbances in a framework given by Tellegen's theorem and adjoint networks
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author shows that power systems subject to large network disturbances can be conveniently analyzed in a framework given by Tellegen's theorem and adjoint networks. The nonlinear AC models are presented and their corresponding accuracy and complexity are addressed for all layers of nonlinearity. Formulas to enable the understanding of the accuracy and complexity are complemented with experimental data. Layer-1 models provide accurate results for most practical cases with a small computational effort. In the few cases in which a more accurate model is necessary, a model still in the same framework will yield any desired accuracy at a competitive price-layer 2 models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Realization of delayed N-path adaptive IIR digital filters
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A delayed N-path structure for high-speed adaptive infinite impulse response (IIR) digital filtering is presented. The strategy adopted for the structural side is to apply the delayed N-path structure to realize each of the numerator and the denominator polynomials of the equation-error-based IIR adaptive digital filtering model. The strategy adopted for the adaptive algorithm is to apply a variable-step method for the adaptive algorithm. Simulation results are included pertaining to using this structure and algorithm for system identifications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of Petri nets to FMS programming systems: K-NET
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors introduce a new mature support system for the development of flexible manufacturing system (FMS) control software, K-NET. The system is based on the Petri net description model combined with a conventional procedural language. This system supports all development stages including high level design, detailed design, programming and testing in a consistent manner. A descriptive model of sequence control by Petri nets has become attractive due to its graphical feature and mathematical formalism. The main advantages of net formalism in FMS control programming are demonstrated. A successful application of K-NET to develop a control system for automated guided vehicles (AGVs) is reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high performance multiprocessor system for image processing applications
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A small, specialized image processing system is presented which is implemented by using a single-chip Intel8031 microcomputer and a Texas TMS32020 microprocessor. With this design the TMS32020 used as a microprocessing unit can provide an efficient implementation of the numeric and pixel-processing capabilities required. The Intel8031 used as the host processor controls all the digitization, storage and display operation. Experiments indicate that this system possesses advantages such as high speed, easy control, and low cost.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new algorithm for calculating the steady-state response of autonomous circuits
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author presents a simple and efficient algorithm for calculating the steady-state response of strongly nonlinear autonomous circuits. The problem is reduced to the solution of an approximating system of nonlinear equations which enables the approximate solution to be directly calculated in the time domain. The numerical procedure is much simpler than those obtained by using either the shooting method or the frequency-domain methods. To demonstrate the usefulness of the proposed algorithm, results are presented for a typical oscillator circuit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A design of CMOS OTA's using simple linearizing techniques and their application to high-frequency continuous-time filters
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A novel CMOS linear operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) with a wide linear input-voltage range is proposed. In this OTA, a simple linearizing technique based on bias-current modulation is adopted to compensate nonlinearities in the transfer characteristic of the conventional current-source-biased source-coupled differential pair. The design and SPICE simulations are presented, assuming implementation by the standard n-well CMOS process. The design and simulated performance of 3.58 MHz OTA-C filter are also given as an application of the proposed OTA.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient method for designing optimal 2-D FIR digital filters with finite wordlength
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A general algorithm for designing finite impulse response (FIR) linear-phase and finite-wordlength 2-D digital filters is presented. The branch and bound technique in conjunction with the I. Barrodale and C. Philips (BP) linear minimax algorithm (1974) is used to solve the discrete variable problem. An approach has been developed which has the important property that once the root node is generated the rest of the subproblems can be solved very efficiently. In some cases it is not even necessary to solve the subproblem to realize that one can stop further branching.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Systolic parasitic insensitive switched capacitor and digital filters
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A systematic method for implementing parasitic-insensitive (PI) switched capacitor filters (SCFs) and digital filters (DIGFs) using systolic array architecture (SAA) is introduced. A signal flow graph (SFG) method is used for a general treatment of first and second order filters. Systematic reduction of the SFGs leads to a number of SAA implementations which will require minimal hardware. Practical aspects of implementation are discussed. Simulation results are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integral transforms as a change of basis in a vectorial space
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The value of the signal in one point of the variable is presented as the component of the vector in the basis vector associated with that point. The decomposition of the signal in its components is called the Dirac transform. The change of the convolution into a multiplication, made by the Fourier transform, is a change of bases in the linear space where the signals are defined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: State vector estimation of high dimensional systems based on functional spline operators
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An estimation procedure based on the functional spline interpolation for dealing with high-dimensional bilinear dynamical models is described. At first, the nonlinear dynamics of a given system is transformed through Carleman bilinearization into a bilinear form. Decoupled bilinear models are then constructed, with input-output mappings expressible in closed form and with dimension determined by the number of training signals used in a prior learning stage. Motivation is given by the need for order reduction and input-output analysis of Carleman bilinearization. An illustration of the technique is made to a forced version of Duffing's equation and merits and eventual extension of the procedure are also highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Relationships among digital one/half band filters, low/high order differentiators and discrete/differentiating Hilbert transformers
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: It is shown that there exists a close relationship among digital one/half band filters, low/high order differentiators, and discrete/differentiating Hilbert transformers. An attempt is made to present a complete picture of their interrelationships and conversions between each other. A table and some block diagrams have been developed for their impulse response connections, and a design example is also given for illustration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Maximization of SNR of filters for optical pattern recognition under the condition of input and detector noise
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Issues involved in the design of optimal filters for optical pattern recognition are discussed. The constraints associated with the implementation of filters using optical devices are outlined. New procedures are presented for the design of complex filters with maximum signal-to-noise ratio in the presence of input noise and detector noise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New methods of moving target imaging and precise ranging
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An imaging method is described which overcomes a defect in the R-D method. The method reduces the demand on the speed of A/D making it convenient for real-time processing. The principles of the imaging method are described, and the radar imaging equation is derived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The mapping of logic designs into a very large scale hardware simulator
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of the ratio cut algorithm used in conjunction with a multistage heuristic in addressing very-large-scale partitioning problems. A very-large-scale system may contain several million gates. To achieve an optimal mapping of such a system onto a fixed hierarchy hardware accelerator presents a formidable challenge to even the fastest computing engines currently available. The authors describe the application of a divide-and-conquer heuristic coupled with the algorithm that solves the problem under a variety of constraints. The goal of this approach is to minimize the communication cost in the hierarchy. The authors describe experiments with designs containing up to two million gates, and demonstrate that the approach decreased communication costs by a factor of two or more, when compared with other approaches. This approach enables the hardware simulator to perform approximately three billion gate evaluations/s, or approximately 200 million event evaluations in an event-driven simulator, using a 6% activity rate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A Urabe type convergence theorem for a constructive simplified Newton method in infinite dimensional spaces
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A constructive simplified Newton method is presented for calculating solutions of infinite dimensional nonlinear equations, which uses a projection scheme from an infinite dimensional space to finite dimensional subspaces. A convergence theorem of the method is shown based on Urabe's theorem. For a class of successive approximation methods containing an infinite dimensional homotopy method, a stopping criterion is shown using the convergence theorem. The authors show that under a certain condition the stopping criterion is satisfied in finite cycles of iteration.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization and simulation of polysilicon TFT-CMOS circuits for HDTV display applications
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Polysilicon thin-film transistors (TFTs) and TFT-CMOS circuits are processed, characterized and modeled for integrated driver applications in high definition display systems. The I-V characteristics of n- and p-channel TFTs are simulated by adjusting the parameters available in a SPICE MOSFET model. The similarities and differences in SPICE simulation of TFTs and MOSFETs are highlighted. The speed achievable in TFT circuits is discussed using time response of basic subcircuits. The performance of static scan drivers and subcircuits is also simulated and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the problem of in-place calculating LPC parameters
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present an in-place procedure for efficiently computing the LPC (linear predictive coding) parameters of a speech signal. The most distinct feature of the in-place deduction is that temporary or scratch-pad registers are not needed for buffering the intermediate results, for the same set of input registers is used as the output registers for holding the recursion results. Therefore, it not only requires small memory size, but also reduces the computation efforts by getting rid of the data transfer operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Verification of error recovery specification for distributed data by using colored Petri net
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: In systems where the same data are distributed in plural memories, it is important for designers to verify that error recovery procedures maintain data consistency after a failure. A modeling and validation method of error recovery specifications by using colored Petri nets is proposed. The analysis of reachable states is useful to consistency. The introduction of the equivalence relation into reachable states reduces the number of the states to be verified. The proposed approach was applied to read/write control of a disk controller with a built-in cache memory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coding of telephone band speech at 5 kbit/s based on glottal excitation analysis
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Application of a separated speech production model in low-bit rate speech coding is studied. The model consists of three parts: the glottal excitation, the vocal tract, and the lip radiation effect. These processes are first estimated with the AIF (adaptive inverse filtering) method. Coding of the glottal excitation is computed as a linear combination of two source signals: an impulse response of a second-order all-pole filter and a noise sequence. Combination of these two source signals is determined using the zero crossings rate of the glottal excitation obtained by the AIF method. The vocal tract transfer function is coded as an LPC (linear predictive coding) filter and the lip radiation effect is modeled with a fixed differentiator. Preliminary results that were obtained when this novel coding method was applied at 5 kbit/s are promising.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Lossy transmission line effects in a thin-film multichip module
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author reports results of an investigation of the chip-to-chip signal propagation properties in a thin-film multichip module. The lossy transmission effects on the CMOS interface were analyzed by SPICE simulation and compared with an emitter-coupled logic interface. It is proved that CMOS-based multichip modules are less affected by the line resistance and have less power dissipation. An example of a CMOS-based multichip module using chip-on-wafer technology is introduced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On improving the linearity of DACs using TIAMPs
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Linearity of a D/A converter using TIAMPs is analyzed. Proof of the fact that DNL at the first-major carry is most sensitive to the gain error of the TIAMPs is given. Results of the linearity analysis lead to an optimum D/A converter configuration using non-identical cells. A TIAMP design with low closed-loop-gain error is described. Experimental results show that accuracy of the TIAMP DAC, limited by channel mismatches of the TIAMPs, has been increased to 11 bits.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Algebraic necessary and sufficient conditions for the stability of 2-D discrete systems
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Algebraic necessary and sufficient conditions for the stability analysis of 2-D discrete systems are presented. These conditions are developed based on the frequency-dependent formulation of the Lyapunov equation using Kronecker products. It is shown that these necessary and sufficient conditions for internal stability of 2-D discrete systems are equivalent to testing the eigenvalues of constant matrices. This is a simplification over earlier tests which require testing the positivity of one or more functions of omega for all omega epsilon (0,2 pi ).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A computational method for the LU decomposition of rectangular matrices and its implications to the realization of 2-D digital filters
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Investigates the realization of 2-D digital filters based on the lower-upper triangular (LU) decomposition of the coefficient matrix. Based on QR decomposition, a novel numerical method that has some important characteristics is proposed to obtain the LU structure. Furthermore, the QR structure can be used for the realization and possesses good numerical characteristics in terms of the approximate realization scheme and the coefficients' values in the structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the implementation of systolic IIR/FIR filters
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two IIR/FIR (infinite impulse response/finite impulse response) systolic arrays with a novel cell architecture are presented together with a comparison of their performance with existing implementations. These arrays are based on the direct form I realization. Bidirectional dataflow is used in both arrays and they still produce one output every cycle with a clock rate unchanged from that of a conventional cell. Type 1 array allows 100% hardware utilization, while type 2 uses one basic cell for FIR and IIR realization.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of adaptive notch filter using multirate technique
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors investigate the steady-state behavior of a multirate adaptive IIR (infinite impulse response) notch filter whose coefficients are estimated using gradient and normalized gradient algorithms. The adaptive detection of a sinusoid with additive Gaussian noise has been investigated. With the help of the obtained difference equations, approximate and simple closed-form results are derived to obtain the mean-square error of coefficient fluctuation for a decimated filter. The present analysis verifies the excellent steady-state performance of the multirate adaptive notch filter recently proposed by M.R. Petraglia et al. (1990). The proposed method of analysis will be useful for the quantitative evaluation for the effects of multirate and block techniques in adaptive notch filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New advances in the routing of mixed analog and digital channels
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A new channel routing algorithm for mixed analog/digital circuits is presented. This router uses two routing layers and is based on a classical vertical constraint graph (VCG) analysis. It is able to handle variable wire width, irregular top and bottom edges, and minimization of crosstalk. To make it more general and to suit the analog designers' needs, some new features have been added: critical nets are routed in one layer if possible and pins may be present on either layer. The problem of cycles in the VCG is also addressed. It is shown that new types of cycles may appear due to analog constraints. The authors describe the proposed solution. Some results obtained on real circuits designed at CNET are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A transmitter chip for an ECG heart rate monitor
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A transmitter chip for a heart rate indicator is being developed. In addition to bandpass filtering, nonlinear circuitry is being used to improve detection reliability under noisy conditions. The decision level for detection adapts to varying signal levels. A complete test chip has been designed and tested. It is integrated using a microwave analog technique and uses continuous-time, switched-capacitor, and digital circuitry. The detection principle, blocks used in implementation, and test results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Flexible capacitor and switch generators for automatic synthesis of data convertors
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two flexible and technology-independent module generators providing very compact and high performance realizations of binary weighted capacitor (BWC) and scaled switch (SS) arrays have been implemented. These generators are general enough to become a powerful tool in layout compilers for binary-weighted-capacitors-based analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) and digital-to-analog converters. Currently, they have been successfully used in a CAD system for automated synthesis of successive approximation ADC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast converging adaptive IIR LMS filter in direct form using the suboptimal step-size
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The concept of adaptive noise cancelling is investigated by employing an adaptive IIR (infinite impulse response) digital filter in direct form with a simplified coefficient-updating algorithm. One of the drawbacks of this adaptive IIR LMS (least mean square) filter in direct form was the difficulty in choosing the step-size for fast coefficient updating. Initially, the optimal step-size is derived by using the output-equation-error technique. Simulations show that the adaptive IIR filter in direct form with the suboptimal step-size outperforms the output-equation-error technique. In connection with the problem of stability of the adaptive IIR filter considered, it is shown that with the suboptimal step-size the coefficient updating algorithm is very robust. In particular, a commonly used stability test prior to new coefficient adjustment is basically no longer required.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Neural networks for digital adder
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A description is presented of a binary adder using the Hopfield type neural network in which false operations due to local minimum equilibria are avoided. Emphasis is placed on the procedure to correct the false operations by introducing stable conditions of a neuron cell. In addition to this binary adder, the Hopfield type adder with a carry-look-ahead circuit is described. Furthermore, the construction of the proposed adder using CMOS inverters is described. The simulation results show that the proposed adder can achieve high performance operation because of an almost constant operation time, regardless of increase in the number of bits in the circuit.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effects of parasitics on distributed high-pass MOSFET filters
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The effects of parasitic capacitances on distributed high-pass MOSFET filters are investigated. Three schemes of MOSFET configurations functioning as distributed high-pass filters are analyzed to demonstrate the parasitic effects. It is found that one high-pass configuration is superior to the other two. It maintains the high-pass characteristics regardless of the effects of parasitic capacitances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A cutset approach to survivability evaluation of large telecommunication-networks with heterogeneous link-capacities
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present a computer approach to compute the survivability of a telecommunication network having heterogeneous link capacities. The survivability measure has been defined as capacity related reliability (CRR). The authors provide a new technique to generate the CRR. The proposed method requires the cutset information of the network. Modified power sets (MPSs) for each cut are generated. An MPS is a subset of a cut which is able to block a transmission message of size W/sub min/ between a given source and destination node pair. From the generated MPSs the method obtains an expression for a capacity related unreliability (CRU), and CRR=1-CRU. The proposed MPS algorithm has been implemented in C on a SUN Wafer computer system. The authors utilized the MPS method to generate the CRRs for some telecommunication networks with various W/sub min/ values, and they compare the results with previous results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improving the performance of CELP-based speech coding at low bit rates
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors review the CELP (code excited linear prediction) coding algorithm, and the efforts recently made for improving the performance and reducing the complexity. The efforts for improving the coding performance have been aimed not only at making the quality better, but also at further reducing the bit rate without degrading the quality. A sparse-delta codebook is introduced as an example of a codebook with a computationally efficient structure. Multimode coding is then described for improving the perceptual quality of CELP at low bit rates.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A realization method of three-dimensional digital filters
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The author proposes a method for realizing three-dimensional digital filters (3DDFs) by the state space method. If one extends the past methods for realizing two-dimensional digital filters to 3DDFs, complicated matrix calculation (canonical decomposition of variable coefficient state equations) is necessary or enormous equations have to be solved. Therefore, in the present work, the denominator and numerator of the given 3DDF are realized independently. By using this method, the above-mentioned difficulties can be avoided. The authors also show that the separable-denominator 3DDF can be realized with a minimal dimension with respect to two variables.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A learning and forgetting algorithm in associative memories: results involving pseudo inverses
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors develop a design technique for associative memories with learning and forgetting abilities via artificial feedback neural networks. The proposed method utilizes the theory of large-scale dynamical systems, instead of the usual energy methods. Networks synthesized by this design method are capable of learning new patterns as well as forgetting existing patterns without the necessity of recomputing the entire interconnection weights and external inputs. The method employs the properties of pseudo-inverse matrices to iteratively solve systems of linear equations, and provides significant improvements over the outer product method and the projection learning rule. Several specific examples are given to illustrate the strengths and weaknesses of the methodology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and implementation of sigma-delta D/A converters with optimized loop filters
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: Two novel procedures are presented for the design of optimum loop filters for oversampling D/A converters. FIR as well as IIR systems are proposed for this purpose. Whereas the nonrecursive filters can be implemented more easily in combination with the interpolator, the recursive ones shows better results in terms of the desired noise suppression for a given oversampling ratio. Stable modulators of arbitrary order can be designed with any desired number of quantization levels at the output. Examples of practical implementations are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: First-order theory of symmetrical reciprocal lossless six-port
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present the derivation of the relationships existing between the various scattering coefficients of a symmetrical reciprocal lossless six-port. Only small departures of the scattering-coefficient values from the ideal design specifications of zero mismatch, zero coupling between certain ports, and equal coupling amongst the other ports are considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Tomographic reconstruction using optoelectronic architecture
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A novel approach for implementing tomographic reconstruction algorithms using optoelectronic CCD (charge coupled device) structures is described. The approach employs the algebraic reconstruction technique (ART). The proposed method overcomes the problems of poor reconstruction results and implementation difficulties traditionally associated with ART. The optoelectronic approach described offers significant advantages over existing electronic methods both in terms of computational speed and quality of reconstruction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fuzzy neuron and its application to a hand-written character recognition system
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A fuzzy neuron in which weighting factors and summation of a conventional neuron model are modified by a membership function and fuzzy logic functions, respectively, is described. An inhibitory synaptic junction is represented by a fuzzy logic complement. This fuzzy neuron facilitates a pattern recognition of a hand-written character by only one layer. It is verified by constructing the pattern recognition hardware system. The distinctive features of this system are: (1) its simplicity of design, (2) its robustness against noises and defects in the pattern, and (3) its high speed (500 ns).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An extension of the Lienard theorem and its application (nonlinear circuits)
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: The authors present a theorem asserting the existence of a unique stable periodic solution of the differential equation d/sup 2/x/dt/sup 2/+f(x)dx/dt+ g(x)=0 under the same conditions as those of the well-known Lienard theorem, except for the condition for f(x) and g(x) in the Lienard theorem replaced by the condition that they are respectively not necessarily even and odd with respect to x. Also, as a simple illustrative example, the extended theorem is applied to an oscillator circuit consisting of L, C, R, a tunnel diode, and a battery. A criterion of the existence of stable oscillation is given with respect to the range of a DC bias.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fault detection and diagnosis based on signature analysis
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An examination is made of widely accepted assumptions underlying the analysis of aliasing phenomena and related problems when using linear feedback shift registers. An extensive fault simulation has been used as a tool to collect the required data characterizing the behavior of these circuits together with the test response compactors implemented by LFSRs and MISRs. At least five million test vectors have been simulated and more than 15000 faults have been analyzed in order to obtain the realistic values of such quantities as the fault coverage after compaction, the aliasing probability as a function of a number of tests applied or the number of times a fault is detected, and the histograms of aliased faults. It is shown that the theoretical models of compaction procedures using LFSRs or MISRs yield results very close to those obtained from experiments performed in the fault domain.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Common VLSI architecture for a practically useful residue number system
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: An architecture is presented for carrying out modulo arithmetic in a practically useful residue number system. An important feature of this is that it allows a single hardware design to be used for all moduli. An application of this architecture is described for computing inner-products in convolutions, transforms and matrix-vector operations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A neutral net linear programming solver
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A linear programming solver which can find the optimal solution for primal-dual linear programming (PDLP) problems is presented. The neural net solver is based on an extension model of the Kosko's bidirectional associative memory (BAM). The proposed neural net solver uses the same number of neurons and connections as does the Hopfield model or Chua's canonical nonlinear programming model while it resolves the problems of (1) getting infeasible solutions and (2) employing a large penalty term in the objective function. Simulation results based on RC-active circuit implementation of the neural net solver are presented. The results indicate that when the solver is implemented in hardware with full parallelism, it is capable of solving linear programming problems very quickly and this computation speed seems to be insensitive to the dimension of the underlying problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analogue layout synthesis based on a planning scheme using artificial intelligence
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A hierarchical planning scheme is presented for the layout synthesis of analogue VLSI circuit. The expert system developed using this technique has proved to be a very powerful and flexible approach for solving the problems which are unique to the analogue VLSI domain. The case study example gave a detailed insight to the general working of the expert layout system developed for dealing with the design intricacies of analogue VLSI design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On counter-based compaction
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: A study is made of the three most popular counter-based compaction schemes, i.e., one's counting, transition counting, and edge counting. For one's counting, using the asymmetric error model, equations for iterative computations of exact aliasing probability for any test session length are derived, and the asymptotic probability of aliasing is determined. Also presented is a closed form expression that, for any test session length, gives the exact aliasing probability. Some examples that compare the aliasing by counter-based compaction with that by linear feedback shift registers are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of super high definition image processing on HiPIPE
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
abstract: In order to manipulate SHD (super high definition) images, a novel parallel processing unit called HiPIPE (Highly Parallel Image Processing Engine) is developed as a project of NOVI-II. The engine is connected to an SHD image display unit and an image data storage unit. Extremely high computational power is obtained by a multicomputer type parallel processing technique. 128 processing elements are connected by a mesh network. Various image coding schemes are carefully explored from the viewpoint of parallel processing, and the problem of processor connections is examined. A novel load-balancing technique, called 2-dimensional butterfly data shuffling, is developed and implemented. The current version of HiPIPE uses just 128 scalar processing elements and has more than twice the power of a single-processor CRAY-2 for a still SHD image coding task.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some recent applications of high-level Petri nets
publicationTitle: 1991 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
